members.note: the decoder's ctor only: Packet.generatePacket instantiates it by reflection (newInstance) for bytes read off a socket (MessageDeserializer); the integrated server's local channel passes packet objects with no codec (NetworkManager.provideLocalClient adds only the packet_handler), so it never runs

notes: EntityLivingBase.onUpdate compares each equipment slot with previousEquipment after onEntityUpdate and before onLivingUpdate and sends an S04 for each change; EntityTrackerEntry.tryStartWachingThis sends the whole equipment at the tracker's first contact. Natively living_on_update keeps equip_sent (the slots as that pass saw them); the live client's copy (clientents.c) takes the equipment at its spawn and each row's equip_sent at the next client tick, which is what it draws (play.c's mob pass). A change onLivingUpdate makes (a witch's potion, a pickup) thus reaches the copy two frames later. idx-clientview-s1 (a witch drinking fire resistance) holds the copy's equipment to the oracle client's at every frame: the server's own equipment drawn fails at row 277.
